reason: Based linear attention: a 2nd-order Taylor feature map (1 + qk + (qk)^2/2), chunked, with intra-chunk masked attention and inter-chunk prefix sums of 1st- and 2nd-order KV states (dk^2 x dv), plus a cumsum normalizer. It has no decay and its feature map and state differ from retention's gamma^(i-j)-decayed QK^T with abs-sum normalization, so the math is materially different.
fixup: consistency with hedgehog_linear_attention: causal chunked linear attention (feature-map phi(q)phi(k)^T, intra-chunk mask + inter-chunk prefix state) is 15p's retention kernel with gamma=1

reason: The core is causal linear attention, (phi(q)phi(k)^T masked causally) V, divided by the row sum of the scores. That is 15p's retention with gamma=1 and a slightly different normalizer clamp. The Hedgehog feature map (a d x d linear plus softmax on q and k) is a cheap prologue next to the chunked attention, so the rest differs only in constants and pre-processing.

Core is non-causal MHA softmax(QK^T*scale + bias)V over N=1024 tokens, with qkv/proj linears and a query-dependent decomposed 2D rel-pos bias (q.Rh + q.Rw) added to the scores. The rubric lists rel-pos bias as keep, but 5p's score mod is exactly an additive rel-pos bias, so this is the same flash-attention-with-additive-bias kernel. The only differences are that the bias is computed in-kernel from q and there is no causal mask.

This is Swin attention: roll, partition into 7x7 windows, per-window MHSA over 49 tokens with a relative-position bias gathered from a table and an additive shift mask, then window reverse. The qkv/proj GEMMs and the window layout dominate the cost. Tiny-window attention with a gathered rel-pos bias and shift masking is materially different from long-sequence flash/flex attention.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: attention with a bias/mask/score-mod = 5p

reason: Causal GQA softmax attention, but each logit is sum_d q_id k_jd 2^(P_id - P_jd) with cumsum per-channel log-sigmoid gates, plus a data-dependent scalar decay bias and a sink term in the denominator. The per-channel gating sits inside the dot product, so the core is not a plain QK^T matmul or an additive score mod, and a flash kernel would need GLA-style chunk rescaling.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: attention with a bias/mask/score-mod = 1p/2p

reason: The softmax is over the feature axis, so there is no QK^T and this is not attention. It is a position-wise gated MLP: three up-projections, then sigmoid(q)*softmax(k)*v, then a down-projection. That has the same fused up-gate-down structure as SwiGLU, with an extra branch and a row softmax, and I can't tell whether that counts as the same algorithm.
swapaxes, then x @ w + b, then swap back. That is a plain linear layer with a bias add (a GEMV, since out_features=1). The rubric maps a plain linear with at most a bias to 8p.

Single-head softmax(QK^T)V whose scores are modified elementwise by a dense per-batch (n,n) mask (scores*mask - P*(1-mask)), the same as 5p's score_mod. The rest is ReLU(Linear+bias) Q/K/V/out projections, which is 41k's Gemm+Add+ReLU chain, so nothing in it lies outside the benchmark.

Q, K, V and output projections are plain GEMM+bias+ReLU (41k-style) around a single-head softmax(QK^T)V whose scores are modified by a dense mask tensor (score*m - P*(1-m)), which is a flex-style score mod. Every substantial part is a benchmark algorithm and there is no other block component.

Soft-target CE: -mean(target * log_softmax(x)) over the 128-wide channel axis of NCHW, with no fused linear and no integer-label gather. It shares 13p's logsumexp-over-classes core, but the rubric puts label smoothing at borderline and KL at keep, and dense soft-target CE sits between them.

Plain non-causal single-head softmax(F G^T) H over HW=4096 tokens (head dim 128) is about 89% of FLOPs. The instance norm and 1x1 conv+ReLU6 projections around it are standard attention pre/post-processing, so the core is 1p's SDPA.

A single Luong-general attention layer. The learned matrix is only a query projection, followed by plain non-causal softmax(xK^T)V with K=V=src, then concat, an output projection and tanh. The only non-GEMM kernel is plain dot-product attention; the projections are packaging around it.

Luong 'general' attention, but q = query@W_in only makes the scores plain QK^T with K=V=context. The core is unscaled non-causal softmax(QK^T)V (about 137 GFLOP of about 240). The concat, output Linear and tanh are trivial post-processing, and returning the weights does not change the algorithm.

argmax over the label tensor gives integer targets, followed by log_softmax over the 128-class axis, an NLL gather and a mean. That is standard softmax cross-entropy with integer targets; only the layout (class axis 1) and the argmax preprocessing differ.

Two 1x1x1 Conv3d layers are just a pointwise Linear -> exact GELU -> Linear MLP over channels, with NCDHW<->NDHWC transposes. All FLOPs are 8p-style GEMMs with a bias/activation epilogue, and the fused up->act->down structure is 9p minus the gate.
Concat of two feature tensors, then a single Linear (8192x4096x1024 GEMM) plus bias. That is a plain matmul with a bias add after a trivial concat, i.e. 8p's algorithm.

The core is row-wise log_softmax over logits, then -sum(labels * log_probs), averaged over the batch. That is the same formula as 13p's one_hot * log_probs, with the one-hot labels passed as a dense tensor. The missing linear does not matter, since the rubric maps plain CE over logits to 13p.

The op chain is 13p's CE tail (log_softmax over classes, one_hot of integer targets, multiply, mean). But the torch-style broadcast puts the (N,C) one-hot against the (H,W) axes, so the effective math sums -log_softmax over all classes at gathered spatial positions instead of picking the target logit. Same op chain, different effective computation, so I can't place it cleanly.

Standard softmax cross-entropy: log_softmax over the class axis, gather at integer labels, mean NLL. The labels come from an argmax of a dense target, which is trivial preprocessing, and the class axis being dim 1 is a layout difference, so this is the rubric's plain-CE -> 13p case.

Standard nn.MultiheadAttention: Q/K/V in-projections, non-causal 4-head scaled softmax(QK^T)V, out-projection. That is the 1p/2p algorithm with standard projections. Caveat: the value is a latent broadcast over S, so the output does not depend on Q and K, but the reference still computes full SDPA.

A full transformer decoder layer: masked self-MHA, cross-MHA, three LayerNorms and a 1024->4096->1024 ReLU FFN. The QK^T/PV attention is about 34 of roughly 240 GFLOP, so it is one part among several substantial ones.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: full softmax attention is a substantial part of the core

reason: One shared Linear (x @ W + b) applied across a leading channel axis, then swapaxes(0,1). That is a plain GEMM with a bias add and an output transpose, i.e. 8p with trivial pre/post-processing.
The workload is exactly data @ w + b over the last axis (M=262144, K=N=256): a plain linear with a bias add, which is 8p's algorithm.

Three stacked dense GEMMs: Linear+bias+ReLU twice, then Linear+bias. Each of the first two layers is exactly 41k's Gemm->Add->ReLU chain and the last is 8p with a bias, with nothing else in the problem.

The cost is a stack of 7 large batched GEMMs (8 ensembles x 8192 x 1024 x 1024), each with a bias add and a SiLU epilogue. That is the Matmul+bias+Swish algorithm repeated, with only a trivial input normalisation and softplus clamps around it.

An ungated two-layer MLP: Gemm+bias+ReLU (exactly 41k's op chain), then Gemm+bias (8p) and an elementwise mask multiply. All the work is GEMMs with trivial epilogues, and the fused up-act-down design is 9p's minus the gate.

Filter Response Normalization without TLU is x * rsqrt(mean(x^2 over H,W) + |eps|) * gamma + beta. That is the RMSNorm formula, here over the contiguous trailing HW axis per (b,c) row. The only differences from 12p are shapes, per-row rather than per-column scale, and a bias add, all trivial.

Linear -> tanh-GELU -> Linear: a fused up-activation-down MLP. It has the same kernel design as 9p (tile the hidden dim, accumulate the down-projection) but no gate, and each half is a GEMM+epilogue like 44k. I can't decide whether the ungated MLP counts as the same algorithm.

FLOPs are dominated by a non-gated up-ReLU-down FFN (1024->4096->1024), wrapped in add+LayerNorm before and residual+LayerNorm after. The fused up/act/down kernel design matches 9p minus the gate GEMM (and its first half is 41k's Gemm+Add+ReLU chain), but it is not gated, so I can't call it the same algorithm or clearly different.

CONFIG sets gamma=0.0 and alpha=1.0, so the focal factor (1-p)^0 is exactly 1. What remains is mean -log_softmax over the class axis gathered at integer targets, which is plain softmax CE. The leftover softmax on the gathered slice is dead work.
Bias-free Linear followed by LeakyReLU(0.1). It is 20k's GEMM + LeakyReLU chain minus the constant multiply and bias, i.e. 8p plus one activation.
A single matmul followed by LeakyReLU(0.1), which is 20k's GEMM->LeakyReLU chain minus the bias and constant multiply. Per the rubric it is a plain matmul with one activation.

relu(x@Wh+b) * sigmoid(x@Wg+b) is the fused dual-GEMM gated-unit stage that makes up 2/3 of 9p's FLOPs, with only the activations changed. However, it has no down projection, which is a missing stage rather than trivial post-processing.

Three large compute-bound GEMMs (131072 rows, 512->1024->1024->512), each with only a bias add and one activation (ELU, sigmoid, none). That is the plain GEMM algorithm with trivial epilogues, repeated.

Non-local block: theta/phi/g 1x1 projections, then plain non-causal single-head softmax(theta phi^T) g over 4096 tokens (head dim 256), then an output projection and residual. The attention is about 80% of FLOPs and the rest is standard q/k/v/o projection, so the core is plain SDPA.

A Set Transformer ISAB: two stacked MAB blocks, each with Q/K/V projections, non-causal multi-head attention (128 inducing points against 4096), a residual, and a ReLU FC residual. Projections and FCs are ~80% of FLOPs, so attention is one part of a multi-part block.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: full softmax attention is a substantial part of the core

reason: Two Set-Transformer MAB blocks (projections, MHA, residual, relu-FC residual). The MHA has only 128 inducing points on one side, so attention is about 5% of FLOPs and needs no long-KV flash tiling. Attention is a minor part of a larger block dominated by projections and FCs.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: full softmax attention is a substantial part of the core

reason: Because stride equals kernel size, the transposed conv has no overlap and is literally one einsum GEMM (M=B*L, K=Cin, N=Cout*K) plus a bias add and an output reshape. The conv framing hides a plain matmul with bias.

ConvTranspose1d with stride == kernel_size has no overlapping taps, so it is exactly one matmul (contract C_in: (B*L x C_in) @ (C_in x C_out*K)) plus a bias add, with the K taps interleaved into the output length. That is a plain matmul+bias with a layout reshape.

x (B,I) shared across C channel weights (C,I,O) plus a per-channel bias. This equals one dense GEMM x @ W.reshape(I, C*O) plus a bias in a (C,B,O) layout, i.e. a plain matmul with a bias add. It is not grouped, since x is the same for every channel.

Q/K/V projections feed a standard non-causal 4-head softmax(QK^T)V over 2048x2048, which is about half the FLOPs and the S^2 memory problem. The extras are a different scale constant (sqrt(dim_V)), a Q residual and one relu-linear residual. The attention core is 1p's algorithm.

A single max-pooled query per batch attends over T=2048 keys, then the outputs and head-averaged weights are broadcast T times. Cost is the K/V in-projection GEMM plus large broadcast writes; the attention is a negligible single-query pooling step with no SxS score matrix or flash tiling.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: full softmax attention is a substantial part of the core

reason: Three chained matmul+bias+tanh layers, so each layer is a GEMM with one activation (8p/k-style). The widths are tiny (128->40->40->4), though, so the real kernel is a memory-bound, per-row fused MLP chain that no compute-bound benchmark GEMM resembles. Shapes alone should not decide it, so I can't call it either way.

Gemm -> LayerNorm(affine) -> SiLU -> Gemm+bias. The first half is essentially 45k's Gemm -> GroupNorm -> Swish epilogue (LayerNorm is a 1-group GroupNorm) and the second is an 8p GEMM. The row-norm between the two matmuls is a non-trivial reduction and not an exact k-task chain, so I can't call it either way.

Three chained Linear(+ReLU) layers (512->1024->1024->512) over 65k rows. Each layer is exactly the 41k GEMM+bias+ReLU chain (the last is 8p), so it is the same algorithm stacked. It is not a single k-chain and has no gate, so I'm unsure whether stacking counts.

A standard MHA layer: Q/K/V projections, plain non-causal scaled softmax(QK^T)V over 16 heads, output projection, residual and LayerNorm. The projections are plain GEMMs (8p) and the attention core is 1p's SDPA; returning the attention probabilities forces materializing them, but the algorithm is unchanged.

Fused QKV linear, non-causal 4-head scaled softmax(QK^T)V, out projection, residual add, LayerNorm. SDPA is about two-thirds of FLOPs at seq 2048, and the rest is standard projection, residual and LayerNorm pre/post-processing, so the core is 1p's algorithm.
Plain non-causal multi-head attention in a channel-first layout: K^T Q scores scaled by 1/sqrt(d), a softmax over the key axis, then V times weights. That is softmax(QK^T)V up to transposes.
Plain non-causal single-head softmax(Q K)V with a residual add (q + attn@v); K is a reshaped view of the same buffer as V. That is unscaled SDPA, which the rubric maps to 1p.

After cheap L2 normalization, the core is a 4096^3 matmul z1 @ z2^T, an elementwise scale by exp(t), and softmax cross-entropy with integer targets (arange, so the target logit is the diagonal): logsumexp minus the target logit. That is fused linear + softmax-CE with trivial pre/post-processing.

Despite the conv framing, 1x1-conv Q/K/V feed softmax over keys of K Q^T, then a weighted sum of V over N=4096 spatial positions. That is plain non-causal single-head softmax(QK^T)V (unscaled), which dominates FLOPs (about 69 of 103 GFLOP). The 1x1 projections and residual are pre/post-processing.

The dominant einsum 'bkf,ekf->bke' is a uniform grouped/batched matmul with pairs as groups, which is the same pattern as 14p's 'gmk,gkn->gmn'. It is wrapped in a triu pair-gather prologue and a fused dot-with-q epilogue that collapses the output to (B,P). I can't cleanly call that gather/bilinear wrapper trivial or substantial.

Softmax spatial attention (N=4096, d=128) is about a third of the FLOPs. The rest is three 3x3 reflect-pad convs, mean-variance norms, 1x1 projections and a gated multi-scale conv fuse. Attention is one part among several substantial parts.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: full softmax attention is a substantial part of the core

reason: 1x1 convs (plain linears) produce Q/K/V, then plain non-causal softmax(QK^T)V over N=4096 positions with head dim 128, then an output 1x1 conv and a residual add. The S x S attention dominates FLOPs and is standard SDPA.
x * rsqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) is exactly RMSNorm without the scale weight. Reducing over axis 2 instead of the last axis is a layout/reshape difference only.

DANet position attention: 1x1-conv projections, softmax over j of C^T B (N=4096 positions, inner dim 512), D @ S^T, then alpha * out + A. That is single-head non-causal softmax(QK^T)V in channel-first layout with no scale, and it dominates FLOPs (about 84%). The residual and layout are trivial differences.
The quant stubs are identity, and the swapaxes do not touch the contracted last axis, so the workload is x @ w + b: a plain linear with a bias add, which is 8p's algorithm.

relu(x)@W0+b0 -> relu -> @W1+b1 -> +x: two dense GEMMs whose only extras are a bias, one ReLU each and a residual add. That is plain 8p-style linears with trivial pre/post-processing; a non-gated version of the 9p MLP with nothing else substantial.

ReLU -> Linear -> ReLU -> Linear plus an identity residual: a plain two-layer MLP. All FLOPs are 8p GEMMs with bias/ReLU epilogues, and the residual add is trivial. Its fused up->act->down structure is 9p without the gate.
Two large GEMMs (65536 x 1024 x 1024), each with a bias add and ReLU, plus an identity residual. It is the GEMM+bias+ReLU algorithm twice, a non-gated MLP, with no other substantial component.

Set Attention Block: Q/K/V projections, non-causal 4-head softmax(QK^T/sqrt(dim_V))V, then a residual q + attn and O + relu(fc_o(O)). Attention dominates FLOPs at N=2048. The different scale constant and the small residual/FC epilogue are trivial.

Mean-variance norm and 1x1 convs, then single-head non-causal softmax(fg^T)h over 4096 positions with d=512, then an output conv and a residual. The attention is ~80% of FLOPs and is plain softmax(QK^T)V; the rest is light pre/post-processing.

For each (b,i), Q(128x128) @ K-slice -> scale -> softmax -> @V. This is plain non-causal scaled dot-product attention; the torch transpose(1,2) only changes which axis of k is read as the key matrix, a layout detail.

It contains an unmodified softmax(A^T A)A self-attention (Q=K=V=agg, D=512), which points to exclude. But bytes are dominated by the max+sum pooling over dim 1 (about 67 MB read against about 8.6 GFLOP), and the (D,1) output projection collapses the AV matmul into a GEMV. I can't call it either the same as 1p or materially different.

A learned linear scorer (H->1 GEMV) plus an additive mask, softmax over T, then a weighted sum of the same input. This is memory-bound attention pooling with K=V=x and no query sequence: O(T*H), not softmax(QK^T)V between two sequences, and without the paging and GQA that define 6p.
fixup: consistency with kbkc: attention pooling with a value aggregation is softmax(qK^T)V with Lq=1 (decode-like SDPA)

reason: Multi-head self-attention: QKV projections, k^-0.25 scaling of q and k (equivalent to the usual 1/sqrt(d) scale), non-causal softmax(QK^T)V over seq 2048, then an output linear. The attention FLOPs dominate; this is plain MHA SDPA.

nn.MultiheadAttention: packed QKV GEMM, plain non-causal scaled softmax(QK^T)V over 32 heads (seq 2048, head dim 128), and an output GEMM. Every component is a JAXBench algorithm (8p projections, 1p SDPA).

SAGAN-style self-attention: 1x1-conv q/k/v, s = f^T g, softmax over axis 1 (keys for each output position m), h @ beta, gamma * o + x. This is single-head non-causal SDPA (qk dim 128, v dim 512) over 4096 positions in transposed layout, and the attention matmuls dominate FLOPs.
Q/K/V linear projections followed by plain non-causal scaled softmax(QK^T/sqrt(dk))V. This is the textbook single-head SDPA layer.

QKV linears followed by single-head non-causal softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V over T=2048, with head_dim 1024. Attention dominates FLOPs (~275 vs ~206 GFLOP for the projections), and it is the 1p algorithm with a different head count/dim and no mask.
Same pattern as SelfAttentionPooling: a linear D->1 scorer, softmax over the sequence, and a weighted sum of the inputs. It is a single learned-vector pooling reduction, not QK^T-based attention.
fixup: consistency with kbkc: attention pooling with a value aggregation is softmax(qK^T)V with Lq=1 (decode-like SDPA)

reason: Cosine-similarity soft quantization: l2-normalized inputs against a fixed 1024-entry l2-normalized codebook (keys = values), softmax, reconstruction. An entropy loss then needs log_softmax of the probabilities and a global column-sum across all rows. The rubric keeps cosine attention, and the extra global loss pass changes the kernel.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: full softmax attention is a substantial part of the core

reason: Attention pooling: scores m@w with one learned query vector, a softmax over seq, then a weighted sum of m. Mathematically it is softmax(qK^T)V with a single query and K=V (decode-shaped), but the kernel is a memory-bound GEMV + online-softmax pooling, not 1p's tiled QK^T. I can't cleanly place it on either side.
Attention pooling: a matvec score M@w, softmax over seq, then a weighted sum of M. There is no query matrix or QK^T; it is a memory-bound matvec + softmax + reduction rather than flash attention.
fixup: consistency with kbkc: attention pooling with a value aggregation is softmax(qK^T)V with Lq=1 (decode-like SDPA)

reason: Linear -> ELU -> Linear: a plain two-layer MLP whose FLOPs are all 8p GEMMs with bias plus one activation. It is the 9p up->act->down structure minus the gate.

The whole problem is Sinkhorn normalisation: 100 alternating row/column logsumexp updates of exp((-C+u+v)/eps), then pi and the transport cost. The rubric maps Sinkhorn to 56p explicitly, even though 56p runs it in the probability domain on 4x4 matrices.

Soft-target CE: -log_softmax(x) over the 128-wide channel axis, weighted by an (H,W) target broadcast over batch and channels, then summed. It shares 13p's per-row logsumexp core but has no integer labels and no fused linear. As with AttentionCrossEntropy, soft-target CE sits between label smoothing (borderline) and KL (keep).

sum(-t * log_softmax(x)) over 512 classes is 13p's CE formula (which literally uses one_hot * log_probs) with dense soft targets and no fused linear. This is the same structure as label-smoothed CE, which the rubric calls borderline.

Row log_softmax over 128 classes dotted with a dense soft-target distribution, then the mean. It is softmax CE, but with dense targets instead of an integer gather and no fused vocab GEMM. That generalises label smoothing, which the rubric marks borderline.

hiddens@W+b -> logsumexp -> gather target logit, which is exactly the fused linear + softmax-CE algorithm of 64p (and 13p). The only difference is a trivial per-token q-log transform (expm1((1-q)*logp)) in place of -logp before the mean.

Non-causal 4-head MHA at seq 4096 (head_dim 512), which needs 1p-style flash tiling, wrapped in bare Q/K/V/out/fc1/fc2 GEMMs and residuals with no norm or activation. Every substantial part is a benchmark algorithm (1p and 8p), so the transformer-block keep clause does not add anything materially different.

The code has no rel_shift, so the 'relative' term is just a second dot product with projected pos_emb. Scores (q+u)k^T + (q+v)p^T equal one QK^T over concatenated head dims [q+u | q+v] x [k | p], followed by a masked softmax from an input mask and AV. That is non-causal MHA SDPA with an input mask, as in the MLA-style two-term score.

QKV linears, a reshape that groups 4 tokens into wider heads, plain non-causal scaled softmax(QK^T)V (the pad mask is inactive at T=4096), and an output linear. It is a standard MHA layer apart from a reshape.

Linformer: K and V are projected along the sequence axis by a shared learned E (2048->256), which is about half the FLOPs and the algorithm's defining step, then softmax attention runs over only 256 compressed keys, which needs no long-KV flash tiling. This is a distinct efficient-attention variant. It is also unlike the DeepSeek-V4 paged compressed-attention tasks.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: attention with a bias/mask/score-mod = 1p

reason: Q/K/V Linear, then softmax(QK^T + learned (L,L) bias)V. That is SDPA with an additive score bias, exactly 5p's relative-position-bias score_mod (non-causal, single head). Returning the probabilities does not change the algorithm.
About 95% of the FLOPs are the first layer, a 2048x16384x256 GEMM + bias + ReLU (exactly 41k's chain). The remaining small Linear+ReLU layers are the same algorithm repeated.

Music Transformer relative attention: QK^T plus relative logits q@E_r^T realigned per row by the pad/reshape skew trick, then softmax and AV. A per-offset relative embedding matmul with a diagonal skew is the rel-pos variant the rubric keeps, not a loaded bias tensor added to SDPA scores.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: attention with a bias/mask/score-mod = 5p

reason: Transformer-XL relative attention: AC = (q + r_w_bias)·k plus BD = rel_shift((q + r_r_bias)·R), a second content-dependent QK-style matmul against positional keys with a skew shift, then softmax, AV, o_net, residual and LayerNorm. 5p adds a static bias tensor, whereas this is a materially different score computation, which the rubric keeps.
fixup: fix-up under the corrected rubric: attention with a bias/mask/score-mod = 5p

reason: Finite scalar quantization: two tiny projections (1024->6 and 6->1024) around a fused tanh-bound, round, normalize and mixed-radix index step. The work is memory-bound and centred on the quantizer, not a GEMM. The scan+matmul flag is wrong: cumprod runs only on the constant levels.

The core is per-level bilinear grid sampling: data-dependent gathers of 4 corners at learned offsets, weighted by a softmax over sampling points. There is no QK^T score matrix, so this is not softmax(QK^T)V and matches no JAXBench algorithm.

Soft MoE: two softmaxes over the same slot logits (dispatch over tokens, combine over slots) form dense slot mixtures, then a per-expert GELU FFN runs on the slots. There is no top-k routing, token gather or gated SwiGLU expert, so it is a different algorithm from 10p. The L2/RMS-style norm is a minor prologue.

It uses the same GQA QK^T and weighted-V matmuls, but softmax is replaced by stick-breaking: logsigmoid weights combined through a reverse cumulative sum along the key axis, plus a remainder-mass output. That is a different normalisation that an online-softmax flash kernel cannot express directly, so it is materially different math.

A linear layer (512->640) feeds per-group argmax code selection, a masked one-hot histogram with perplexity, and a codebook gather. There is no softmax or logsumexp, so it is not CE. The post-processing is far more than a bias or activation, so it is not plain 8p either.

L2-normalizes along the feature axis, takes a batched cosine-similarity contraction, then a max-reduce and a softmax over keys. There is no V aggregation and no scaled dot-product, so it is not softmax(QK^T)V.

x@w gives a size-1 score axis, so the softmax is all ones and the output is just sum(x, axis=4). The work is a memory-bound reduction (plus a dead GEMV). There is no QK^T attention and it matches no benchmark task.

Stand-alone local self-attention: 1x1 q/k/v convs, unfold k/v into k x k windows, add relative-position terms, take a per-channel elementwise softmax(q*k) over window positions and a weighted sum with v. There is no dot product over channels and no softmax(QK^T)V, and the 1x1 convs dominate FLOPs.

A GRU-style cell: four GEMMs whose outputs are combined by sigmoid/tanh gates, a reset gate applied to a GEMM output, and a blend with the state. There is no attention, and the multi-GEMM gating fusion is not a JAXBench algorithm.

Computes Luong-dot scores only: one query vector per batch dotted with A encoder states (a memory-bound batched GEMV), then a softmax. There is no P@V aggregation and no tiled QK^T, so it is not the SDPA algorithm.

A full 2-level U-Net: stacked 3x3 conv+bias+ReLU, maxpool, bilinear upsample, skip concat and a 1x1 conv. Convolutions are on the keep list, and the multi-stage network is not 18k's single conv op chain. The 'attention' flag is only the module name.

Small Linear(128->128) plus clamp, then a softmax over the time axis (not the feature axis) and a normalised weighted sum of a second tensor. This is memory-bound attention pooling with no QK^T or AV matmul, and it does not match any k-task op chain.

A small-N linear layer, then softmax over the pooled axis 1 (across rows of the GEMM output, not across output features), then a weighted average of a separate decision tensor. That is attention pooling with a cross-row reduction, not 38k's row-wise softmax epilogue and not QK^T V attention.

This is additive (Bahdanau) attention pooling: tanh(Linear) GEMM, a GEMV score through a learned vector, masked softmax over the sequence, a weighted sum of inputs, then tanh(Linear). The GEMM supplies most of the FLOPs, but a single learned-query pooling is neither softmax(QK^T)V nor a plain GEMM+bias.

Bahdanau additive attention: a large x@W_x GEMM plus a broadcast decoder-state projection, then tanh, a projection to a scalar, and softmax over T. It returns only the weights, with no QK^T and no weighted sum of V. The rubric keeps additive attention.

The einsum contracts over the sequence axis, so it builds an hd x hd (32x32) channel/cross-covariance attention per head, with softmax over features. It is not T x T softmax(QK^T)V. FLOPs are dominated by the four dense projections around this different attention core.

Bahdanau-style additive attention scores: concat -> GEMM+bias -> ReLU -> dot with v -> softmax over time, with no QK^T and no value aggregation. Cost is a GEMM with a row-reduction epilogue (36k-like), but this is not 36k's or 41k's exact op chain.

The cost is BatchNorm batch statistics over a large NCHW tensor, plus an SE-style avgpool->linear->sigmoid mixture of per-channel affine params. It is a centred norm with sigmoid gating, not RMSNorm, attention or a k-task chain.

Linear+bias+ReLU GEMM, then a GEMV score, mask add, softmax over the sequence and a weighted sum of the input. The first stage matches 41k's chain, but the whole problem is additive attention pooling with a reduction epilogue, not 41k's exact op chain and not QK^T attention.

Additive-attention pooling: Linear -> tanh -> Linear energies, softmax over time per channel, then attention-weighted mean and std. There is no QK^T, and the rubric keeps additive attention and stats pooling.

Bahdanau concat attention: concat[h, enc] @ W, tanh, dot with v, softmax over time, returning only the weights. The score is additive through tanh and cannot be written as QK^T, and there is no V aggregation.

A per-batch dot product of each hidden state with one encoder vector (a GEMV-like reduction), then a softmax over the sequence. There is no multiplication by V and no QK^T tile structure, so it is a memory-bound reduction plus softmax, not SDPA.

Luong-general attention: enc @ W + b, contracted with a per-batch hidden vector, then a softmax over seq. Reassociating to enc @ (W hidden) turns the dominant GEMM into a memory-bound GEMV + softmax, so the kernel is neither 8p's GEMM nor SDPA, and the op chain matches no k-task.
Elementwise BCE-with-logits mean plus a per-channel sigmoid Dice reduction. There is no softmax over classes and no integer-target NLL, so it is a different algorithm from 13p.
Elementwise sigmoid BCE-with-logits mean plus a per-sample soft Dice reduction. This is binary/Dice loss math with no softmax over classes and no integer-target gather, so it is not 13p.
An elementwise sigmoid + binary cross-entropy (clamped logs) reduced to a mean. There is no softmax over classes, so the math differs from softmax CE.

Elementwise sigmoid plus binary cross-entropy against soft float targets with log clamping, mean-reduced. This is a memory-bound elementwise loss, not softmax CE over class logits with integer targets.

A full pre-LN ViT block: LN, QKV projection, non-causal MHA, output projection, residual, LN, and a GELU MLP 768->3072->768. The MLP and projections out-FLOP the attention, so SDPA is one part among several substantial parts, which the rubric's transformer-block example says to keep.

Full pre-LN transformer block: LayerNorm, causal MHA with fused QKV, out projection, LayerNorm, GELU MLP (4x), residuals. At these shapes the non-gated GELU MLP and the projections dominate FLOPs (attention is about 8%), so it is a block with several substantial parts.

A tiny actor-critic MLP: Linear(4->128)+ReLU feeding a 2-way softmax head and a value head, over 4M rows. It is memory-bound streaming of a fused tiny network, not a large GEMM, and its op chain is not 50k's.

A focal-style CE: a softmax over the last axis and a log_softmax over the channel axis, each gathered at the targets, combined with (1-p)^gamma weights. There is no fused linear. The rubric lists focal loss as different math from plain CE.
A squeeze-excitation channel gate: global avg pool, a tiny two-layer MLP, sigmoid, then rescaling the input. The rubric keeps it as a sigmoid gate, not softmax(QK^T)V.
A squeeze-excitation gate (global avg pool, small MLP, sigmoid) broadcast back to the input shape. It is a sigmoid channel gate, not softmax(QK^T)V, and matches no benchmark task.
Pure data movement: a circular pad along H (concat) then a zero pad along W. The paged_kv flag is spurious and no JAXBench task does this.
Negative squared L2 distance from one query to two key sets, an elementwise max, then a softmax. It is a memory-bound distance reduction with no QK^T V contraction.
An elementwise contrastive margin loss ((1-t)p^2 + t*clamp(m-p)^2) followed by a global sum. This is a plain elementwise op plus a reduction, with no softmax or CE.
Purely elementwise contrastive margin loss ((1-t)p^2 + t*relu(m-p)^2) followed by a global sum. Nothing in the benchmark has this algorithm.

A full transformer block (LayerNorm, attention, residual, LayerNorm, GELU MLP) where only the CLS token queries. The attention is a negligible single-query step. Cost is dominated by LayerNorm over all tokens plus K/V projections, which can be folded into the query (scores = h·(Wk q), out = (attn·h)Wv), so the core is not SDPA.

A multi-layer network: an encoder linear, two attention blocks with ReLU'd q/k/v and output linears, and a linear head. The linears dominate FLOPs (~80%). Its attention modulates scores with a dense float mask (s*m - P*(1-m)), so attention is one part among several substantial parts.
A dice loss built from per-class spatial sums of p*m, p^2 and m^2, then a ratio. These are elementwise ops and reductions, and the rubric lists dice loss as keep.
Sigmoid followed by global reductions for the dice loss plus elementwise binary cross-entropy. The rubric keeps dice loss, and there is no softmax CE.
Per-sample Dice coefficient plus binary cross-entropy on probabilities: elementwise products and reductions. Dice/BCE is different math from softmax CE with integer targets.
Sigmoid followed by per-channel sum reductions of p*t and p+t into a Dice ratio. The rubric lists dice loss as different math from softmax CE.
Dice loss: per-sample sums of p*t, p and t, then a ratio and a batch mean. These are plain elementwise reductions, and the rubric explicitly keeps dice loss.
Sigmoid followed by a per-channel dice loss (sum(p*t), sum(p+t)). These are spatial sum reductions, and the rubric lists dice loss as a keep; it is not cross-entropy.

GEMV scoring (Linear n_h->1), softmax over the sequence axis, then an elementwise-weighted sum over the sequence of a 4-D tensor. This is bandwidth-bound attention pooling with no QK^T or AV matmul, so it is not SDPA or any k-task.

A non-gated transformer FFN (Linear, tanh-GELU, Linear) followed by a residual add and per-segment LayerNorm. It has no gate branch or up*act(gate) multiply, so it is not the SwiGLU/GeGLU algorithm of 9p, and two GEMMs with an activation between them are more than 8p's single matmul.

Two graph-attention layers. Scores are additive rank-1 sums (h@a_self + (h@a_neigh)^T) scaled by M, passed through leaky_relu and an adjacency mask, then softmax and aggregation. A sigmoid(ZZ^T) decoder follows. The scores are not QK^T, and the decoder and L2 norm make up a substantial share of the work.
Generalized Dice loss: per-channel sums of t, x*t and x+t, weighted by inverse squared volume. These are reductions with different math from CE.

GRU cell: three GEMMs (x@W_ih, h@W_hh_rz, and a dependent (h*r)@W_hh), sigmoid reset and update gates, a ReLU candidate, then interpolation with h. The gate dependency between GEMMs and the recurrent interpolation are not the up*act(gate)->down SwiGLU structure.

A GRU cell step: GEMMs for the r/z gates, a candidate GEMM on r*h, a gated update, and a broadcast (B,B,H) mask blend that dominates the bytes. The recurrent gating math is not any JAXBench algorithm.
A single elementwise Gaussian exp(-(x-mu)^2/(2 sigma^2)) with scalar parameters. It is a memory-bound elementwise op unrelated to any task; the ssm flag is spurious.

Gaussian-kernel MMD: three 8192x8192 Gram GEMMs (two symmetric) turned into squared distances via row norms, then exp(-d2/s) and global means. The fused GEMM+elementwise+reduce pattern resembles 36k, but the distance/RBF math, symmetric Grams and three-term combination are not that op chain.
Global avg pool of x+y, a dense layer and sigmoid, then a gated blend x*a + y*(1-a). It is a memory-bound SE-style sigmoid gate, not softmax attention.

Memory-bound global average pool over 64x64 spatial positions (about 268 MB read), followed by a tiny 32x512x1024 Linear. The pooling reduction dominates. No JAXBench task is a bare spatial mean, and 39k is dominated by its conv.

The leading per-game GEMM dominates FLOPs, but it is followed by a hidden-expansion mix over the game axis + sigmoid that materializes a (B,128,E) tensor (the byte bottleneck), a second contraction + sigmoid, a vocab GEMM and log_softmax. That is far more than trivial post-processing of 8p.

Cosine-normalised batched similarity GEMMs (512 batches of 256x256, K=128), a temperature softmax, then a symmetric KL divergence between two softmax distributions. KL losses are different math from integer-target CE, and there is no V matmul, so it is not attention either.

clamp(preds) * target, a mean over channels, then -log: an elementwise product and a mean reduction with a log. There is no softmax or logsumexp over classes, so the math is not softmax CE despite the name.

The scores come from a batched GEMM into a 5-D tensor, then a softmax over a small 8-wide axis, then an elementwise weighted sum with values. There is no softmax(QK^T)V contraction, so the kernel is a GEMM plus a memory-bound softmax and reduction.

A dense softmax-weighted mixture of linear experts: x is contracted with all L expert weights (one GEMM with K = in*L), then reduced with dense gate weights. There is no top-k routing, sparsity or SwiGLU expert, so the efficient kernel differs from 10p's.

A narrow three-layer ReLU MLP whose first layer is two branch linears concatenated (a block-diagonal GEMM), at batch 65536 with hidden 128/256. A fused multi-layer chain is not a single GEMM+bias(+act), not a gated MLP, and not 41k's exact op chain.

Narrow 3-layer MLP (128->36->36->1, ReLU, ReLU, sigmoid) over 524k rows. It is memory-bound on reading x and its kernel fuses the whole chain. It is not gated (not 9p), not one big compute-bound GEMM (not 8p or 41k), and not 41k's exact op chain.

A tiny 784->32->10 MLP with ReLU and softmax over 65536 rows. It is bandwidth-bound skinny GEMMs, its op chain (Gemm-Add-ReLU-Gemm-Add-Softmax) is no k-task's exact chain, and it is not a gated 9p-style MLP.

Two independent GEMM+bias projections, then a row-reduction gate (Linear 2H->1) + sigmoid, then a convex blend of the two outputs. The fused gated-blend epilogue is more than the 'at most a bias add' of 8p and matches no k-task chain.

A multi-stage pipeline: 3x3/s2 avgpool, a layout-scrambling permute+reshape, a GELU MLP, nearest x2 upsample, then a full-resolution 1x1 conv (which commutes with the upsample). The MLP is one part among substantial pooling, upsampling and layout stages, so it is not a benchmark algorithm as a whole.

A broadcast batched matmul builds a [P,X,G,I,O] weight tensor, softmax runs over the X (graph/batch) axis rather than the key axis, and the result is an elementwise weighted sum with queries. There is no softmax(QK^T)V contraction, so the structure differs from SDPA.

K/V are compressed to 128 slots by learned softmax pooling. Both the item path and the S x S positional path apply softmax over the query axis (axis=-2), which needs column statistics and so is not online-softmax SDPA. LayerNorm, a dense layer and a residual add follow. The core differs materially from 1p/2p.
Elementwise q*(log q - log p) followed by a global sum, with no softmax or logits. The rubric lists KL losses as different math from CE.

A NALU cell: three GEMMs (x@W, x@G, log|x|@W with W=tanh*sigmoid of params) combined as sig(g)*a + (1-sig(g))*exp(m). It has a log-space multiplicative path and a convex blend and no down projection, so it is not up*act(gate)->down.

NALU: two GEMMs share a tanh*sigmoid-transformed weight, one on x and one in log space (log|x| prologue, exp epilogue), blended by a sigmoid row gate from a GEMV. It is GEMM-heavy, but the multi-path log/exp/gate math is more than a bias or one activation and matches no k-task chain.

Soft-assignment clustering: L2-normalize, a 1x1 conv to cluster logits, softmax over the cluster axis (not over the pixels being summed), then residual aggregation a @ x^T - c*sum(a) and two L2 normalizations. The normalization axis and the residual-to-centroid math differ from attention, and the kernel is mostly memory-bound.
Sums of L1 and MSE losses over mel tensors, plus MSE on scaled durations. These are pure elementwise-difference reductions with no attention at all, so the attention flag is wrong.

1x1 convs, then theta@phi, then softmax over dim=1 (the query index), then contraction over the other index. That computes P^T g (the dV-style contraction), not softmax(QK^T)V, so it needs a two-pass column-normalized kernel rather than flash forward. There is also a conv and residual around it.

VOLO outlook attention: local 3x3 window weights are generated by a Linear on avg-pooled features (no QK^T), softmaxed, applied to unfolded V patches, then fold/scatter-added. This local-window, generated-weight algorithm differs from every attention task.

An elementwise fake-quant of activations (clamp, round) and weights (tanh, max-abs, round), then a 4x4 conv2d plus bias. The rubric keeps convolutions, and this is not 18k's exact op chain (it has a quant prologue and no ReLU).
3x3 average pooling (count_include_pad) followed by zero-padding of the channel dimension. The SSM flag is spurious; this is a memory-bound pooling op that matches no benchmark task.
Elementwise sigmoid-MSE -> sqrt plus a numerically stable BCE-with-logits, both as global means. There is no softmax over classes or integer-target gather, so it is not 13p's CE.
A channel mean, log2, and a mean of log2 combined elementwise. This is a reduction plus elementwise ops, and despite the 'moe' flag it has nothing to do with mixture of experts.

Additive-style scoring (Linear+tanh+Linear(d->1)), softmax, then a broadcast-weighted sum. The softmax runs over a size-1 axis, so the weights are all ones and the output degenerates to a batch-sum, but the computation is a GEMM+tanh epilogue, not SDPA or a plain linear. The reference is also semantically degenerate, which is a separate quality concern.

GEMV scores (Linear C->1), a padding mask, a softmax over time, then a weighted sum over time. It is formally single-learned-query attention with K=V=x, but in practice a memory-bound GEMV-softmax-GEMV pooling with no QK^T matmul or flash-style tiling.
A Linear(H->1) GEMV score, softmax over the time axis, and a weighted sum of values: memory-bound attention pooling with a learned scoring vector. There is no QK^T, so it is not SDPA.

An additive-gated pooling classifier: Gemm+bias+ReLU, a D->1 projection with a sigmoid gate, gating of x, mean over the sequence, then a small ReLU/sigmoid MLP head. The large first GEMM matches 41k's chain, but like the rubric's additive-attention case the scoring, gating, pooling and head make it a different multi-stage computation.

A shared two-layer skinny MLP (196->160->10) on two inputs, then concat, a 20->2 linear and a sigmoid, over 131k rows. It is memory-bound streaming of a fused tiny network with branch/concat structure, not a large GEMM+epilogue.

Additive attention pooling: tanh(Linear(x)) GEMM, dot with a learned vector ua, softmax over the sequence, and an attention-weighted sum of x. A single learned-query additive pooling is neither softmax(QK^T)V nor a plain matmul+bias.
Bahdanau-style additive attention pooling: tanh(Linear(x)) dotted with a vector v, a softmax, then a weighted sum over dim 1. There is no QK^T, and the rubric lists additive attention as keep.
A squared soft dice loss: spatial sums of x*y and x^2+y^2, then the mean of 2I/D. These are reductions, listed as a keep (dice is not cross-entropy).
log_softmax over channels followed by KL divergence (xlogy(t,t) - t*logp) against dense soft targets, with a mean. The rubric lists KL losses as different math from integer-target softmax CE.
A per-pixel 1x1 conv (128->16) + ReLU, a 1x1 conv (16->1) + sigmoid. This is a spatial sigmoid gate, which the rubric keeps; there is no softmax attention.

Channel max/mean reductions, small width/height tanh MLPs gated by softmax, an outer-product tanh map, then x*(att+1). This is a memory-bound spatial gate dominated by reductions and an elementwise multiply, not softmax(QK^T)V.
CBAM spatial gate: channel mean/max -> 2->1 3x3 conv -> sigmoid -> multiply. It is a sigmoid gate, not softmax(QK^T)V, and the rubric lists it as keep.
CBAM spatial gate: channel mean and max, a 7x7 conv (2->1), sigmoid, then multiply into x. It is a sigmoid gate with a small conv, not softmax(QK^T)V, and the rubric explicitly keeps it.
A CBAM spatial gate: channel mean and max, a 2->1 3x3 conv, then sigmoid. It is a sigmoid gate built from reductions and a tiny conv, not softmax(QK^T)V.
A CBAM-style spatial gate: channel mean and max, a Conv1d(2->1, k=7), a sigmoid, then a multiply. It is a sigmoid gate, not softmax(QK^T)V, and the rubric lists it as keep.
Pure memory movement: it drops the padding row of the weight and bias tables and tiles them num_device=1 times. There is no matmul or attention, so it matches no benchmark algorithm.

This is a fast style-transfer CNN, not an attention transformer: reflect-padded convs with InstanceNorm and ReLU, 5 residual blocks, and nearest-upsample convs. It is a multi-layer conv network, much larger than 22k's single conv+IN chain.

Nearest-codebook search: a GEMM-based L2 distance to 1024 codes, argmin, gather, commitment loss and a straight-through output. The GEMM is followed by an argmin reduction over the codebook, not a bias add or a logsumexp/CE, so it is a different algorithm from 8p and 64p, though structurally similar to 64p's fused GEMM-reduction.

Weighted binary CE with logits: an elementwise max(x,0) - x*gt + log1p(exp(-|x|)) loss, weighted sum divided by the sum of weights. There is no softmax or logsumexp over a class axis, so the math differs from softmax CE.
A weighted binary dice loss: sigmoid, then weighted global sums. These are memory-bound reductions, and dice loss is a keep.

GEMV scores against a learned vector, an additive mask broadcast into a 5D tensor, a softmax over the batch axis, then a batched matmul with transposed x. It is a garbled masked pooling with odd broadcasting, not QK^T attention or any JAXBench algorithm.

AFT-Full: exp(pos_bias) @ (exp(K)*V) divided by exp(pos_bias) @ exp(K), gated by sigmoid(Q), with q/k/v/out linears. There is no QK^T score matrix and no softmax over query-key dot products, so it is an attention-free algorithm.

The 'attention' is a causal cumulative average (a prefix mean written as a tril/(t+1) matmul, with no Q/K/softmax), followed by a dominant concat-Linear(2D->2D) and a sigmoid input/forget gating mix. This is neither SDPA nor retention's decayed QK^T, nor a k-task chain.

A per-capsule small-matmul einsum builds u_hat, then 4 routing iterations run: softmax over input capsules, a weighted sum, squash and an agreement update. That is iterative routing-by-agreement, not top-k MoE gating or QK^T attention.

Efficient (linear) attention: K softmaxed over the sequence and Q over features, a global K^T V state (dh x dh), then Q @ KV, wrapped in Q/K/V/O linears. It is non-causal with no decay and no N x N score matrix, so it is neither SDPA nor retention.
CBAM channel gate: spatial mean and max pooling, a shared tiny 2-layer ReLU MLP, sum, sigmoid. The memory-bound pooling dominates, and it is a sigmoid gate, not softmax(QK^T)V.

Unnormalized raw QK^T scores (no softmax over keys) are multiplied by V. A per-head gate is computed from that product and softmaxed over Tq, used to mix the raw score maps, and the result is multiplied by the raw inputs. It is neither softmax(QK^T)V nor top-k MoE.

Bug-faithful attention: the transpose(1,2) on 4D contracts q's feature axis with k's spatial axis, and the softmax runs over the query axis (axis 2) while the PV contraction is over the other axis. Outputs are therefore not convex combinations of values and the flash/online-softmax design does not apply, so it is materially different from SDPA; the projection GEMMs dominate FLOPs.

ConvTranspose2d with k=s=2, done as a per-pixel GEMM (K=256), then bias, a pixel-interleave layout, and a channel concat with x1. It is dominated by the strided output writes and the concat, and the rubric keeps convolutions.
